accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding N1, minor] For an ordinary SCM, every generated variable is observed and nothing is computed during sampling, so these questions only matter for a process that (i) separates latent from observed variables and (ii) computes moments during generation, by population or empirical estimate. Those are exactly the two defining parts of the withheld idea in the target's Sec. 3.1. The grading anchor J1 and the private reference repeat the same wording, which shows the requirement was written around the reference answer. The public text also defines the comparator as standardized 'after sampling'. Together, these give the solver the 'standardize during sampling' angle that the IDEA scope ('must not suggest standardizing inside the generative process') and E2 forbid. Construction note 1 avoided 'post-hoc' for this very reason, but 'after sampling' plus R1 has the same effect. The [B6] heuristic does estimate a sample variance during generation, so the clause is not baseless. But its 'what is observed' and 'population or sample-based' parts go beyond what prior work needs and mirror the target.
Required repair: Reword task.md R1 neutrally, e.g. 'Give equations or numbered sampling steps that take a DAG, mechanisms and noise distributions to n observations, and define every quantity the procedure uses, including any quantity estimated from data, so that another researcher can implement it without further information.' Make the matching change in the schema description of generative_process and in rubric J1's 4-anchor ('unambiguous sampling steps; every quantity used is defined; nonlinear coverage stated'). Optionally shorten the task.md terminology note to 'rescaled to zero mean and unit variance (background report, Section 1)'. Report Sec. 1 already gives the [B1] description. Do not add any substitute hint.
